The problem

Teenagers choose majors based on myths

"Lawyers argue in court every day and make $300k right out of school."

"Game designers play games all day."

"Electricians don't make much money."

Confident, specific, and wrong. Nobody checks them before the student commits years and tuition.

376
students per school counselor (ASCA, 2023–24; recommended 250)
33%
of bachelor's students change major within 3 years (NCES)
The facts are free (BLS + O*NET cover ~800 jobs), but they're dense government tables no teenager reads.

Tokenomics (measured)

A seventh of a cent per student

$0.0015
per exploration (avg of 10 cold runs; 7.9k in / 1.6k out tokens)
−72%
repeat career: cached agents → $0.0004
$1.45
100 students × 10 runs / month
$72–145
10,000 students / month

Cheaper (no reasoning) cost the same and lost a correct verdict; medium reasoning cost +13% and was less accurate (88% vs 94%). We chose low.

Safety

Built for kids, tested with attacks

  • Invented numbers: the validator catches them and the model retries; the student never sees one (caught "$300,000" live)
  • Prompt injection: a free regex layer, then the Gatekeeper
  • Distress: points to a trusted adult and the 988 Lifeline
  • Personal info, off-topic: politely blocked
  • Loops and overspend: per-agent caps; $0.05 per session, $2 per day
  • 8 of 8 live and offline scenarios stopped · 14 automated tests pass
